title: Will and Inheritance
premise: Ulyana Coldharbour, the reclusive archivist of Saltmere Cathedral, has spent years cataloguing the dead while quietly proving that three 'accidental' deaths were murders tied to a shipping fortune built on a drowned crew. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to all three killings, one promising a fourth—Ulyana realizes the confessor knows about his private investigations and is drawing him out. Following a ledger disguised as the cathedral's burial register, he uncovers that his own late father was the paymaster who bought the crew's silence, making Ulyana an heir to both the crime and its cover-up. In the flooded crypt at spring tide, Ulyana confronts the confessor—the last surviving crewman's daughter, who has been killing her way down the ledger—and must choose between exposing the inheritance of guilt, including his own, or letting the sea keep its secrets.
about_author: Freya Delacroix is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade transcribing centuries of baptisms, marriages, and burials in coastal England. Her fascination with what official documents leave unsaid fuels her quiet, archival brand of mystery.

chapters.title: The Register of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. He catalogs the cathedral's burial register on a rain-hung morning, establishing his methodical invisibility among the canons who barely notice him. A passing reference to three drowned men buried without rites plants unease. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine shadowed by the sense that the archive remembers more than people do.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, flashback-tinged. He reviews his private files: a fall from the cliff path, a boathouse fire, a poisoning blamed on bad shellfish—each victim connected to the old Coldharbour Shipping Company. He has solved them but told no one. Emotional beat: the loneliness of knowing things no one asked him to know.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Two letters arrive in the same hand: one confesses to the three deaths in precise detail only the killer could know; the other promises 'a fourth, when the tide is right.' Neither is signed. Emotional beat: cold fear braided with a terrible thrill—someone has finally seen him.

chapters.title: What the Police Were Told
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Inspector Maren Voss, newly transferred, reads the cold-case files and notices the same archivist's name appearing in witness lists across all three deaths. She visits the cathedral under pretense of research. Emotional beat: Voss's professional suspicion meeting Ulyana's practiced blandness—two hunters circling.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. He examines the crypt door's lock, sealed since the 1974 flood, and finds fresh scratches in the salt crust—someone has been inside recently. The confession letter's phrasing echoes words carved into the crypt lintel. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose; the letters are not threats but invitations.

chapters.title: A Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Deciphering marginalia in the burial register, he discovers dates and sums hidden in funeral fees—a payment ledger for hush money to the drowned crew's families, kept by a paymaster whose initials match his father's. Emotional beat: vertigo; the archive he loved has been concealing his own family's guilt.

chapters.title: The Drowned Crew
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She pulls harbor records: the Mary Celestine went down in 1974 with nine hands after the owner ordered an overloaded run; six families were paid off, three never were. The three 'accident' victims descend from unpaid families. Emotional beat: her growing conviction that the accidents are arithmetic—debt being collected.

chapters.title: Confession Without a Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A second letter arrives, confessing again but with details wrong this time—deliberately wrong, he realizes, testing whether he truly solved the cases or merely read about them. He replies through the newspaper's classifieds, correcting the errors. Emotional beat: the intoxication and danger of being known by a killer.

chapters.title: The Canon Who Knew
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Elderly Canon Pell, dying and unburdened, reveals the crypt was sealed not against flood but against scandal: bodies moved during the cover-up, including a crewman buried alive in the panic. Pell gives him a rusted key before slipping away. Emotional beat: grief entwined with complicity inherited secondhand.

chapters.title: Below the Waterline
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, night. Using Pell's key, he enters the flooded crypt at low tide and finds nine niches where there should be none—and a tenth, empty, freshly cleaned, waiting. Emotional beat: claustrophobic terror giving way to horrified understanding: the fourth death is meant to fill it.

chapters.title: The Archivist Suspect
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. An anonymous tip names Ulyana; his private files are found copied onto his office desk, staged as evidence. Voss interviews him and recognizes a man hiding something—but which thing? Emotional beat: mutual recognition between two careful readers of other people's silences.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Ninth Hand
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tracing the ledger's unpaid line, he identifies Edith Marlowe, daughter of the last crewman, presumed lost at sea herself decades ago—yet someone using her mother's maiden name has rented a room above the chandlery. Emotional beat: reluctant empathy; he begins to see the killer as the ledger's final entry, not its author.

chapters.title: What Father Paid
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, interleaved with found documents. His father's paymaster journal surfaces in the archive misfiled as hymnal repairs: entries showing he shorted three families and forged the rest's signatures. Emotional beat: shame crystallizing into resolve—Ulyana will not inherit silence.

chapters.title: The Tide Table
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She maps the letters' postmarks against tide tables and realizes the promised fourth death is scheduled for the highest spring tide of the year—six days away—at a location only readable from the crypt. Emotional beat: racing urgency colliding with institutional skepticism from her superiors.

chapters.title: An Offer of Partnership
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A third letter proposes a bargain: bring the original ledger to the crypt at spring tide and the killing stops; the writer wants only to be witnessed by someone who understands. Ulyana tells Voss everything. Emotional beat: fragile trust formed between archivist and inspector over shared evidence.

chapters.title: Six Days of Salt
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Surveillance, false leads, and a near-miss when Edith slips the constables watching the chandlery. Ulyana decodes the ledger's final cipher: the ninth family was never paid because his father diverted the money—to fund the cathedral's restoration. Emotional beat: mounting pressure as the town's beloved institution is revealed as built on the debt.

chapters.title: The Empty Niche
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. He prepares for the meeting, copying the ledger and writing his own confession—to his silence, his three solved-but-unreported murders, his father's theft. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning; he decides that survival purchased with invisibility has cost too much.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, climax. At high water, Ulyana descends with the ledger while Voss's team seals the cathedral above. Edith appears from the flooded passage—he never left the crypt's other door. She doesn't want money; she wants the ninth name spoken aloud in the nave, restored to the register. Emotional beat: terror dissolving into terrible tenderness between two heirs of the same crime.

chapters.title: The Rising Water
chapters.summary: Climax continued, Ulyana's POV. The tide traps them as the crypt floods faster than expected; Edith means to stay with her father's bones. Ulyana refuses to leave, reading the ninth name and the true ledger aloud as the water climbs, making her the witness instead. Emotional beat: sacrifice inverted—survival offered rather than taken.

chapters.title: What the Sea Gave Back
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Rescue at the last moment; Edith surrenders peacefully, asking only that the record stand. The recovered remains of the ninth hand are raised with the tide's ebb. Emotional beat: exhausted catharsis; the sea, finally, gives up what it took.

chapters.title: Amended Entries
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Trials loom; Ulyana testifies to everything, accepting charges for withholding evidence. The register is amended in red ink—nine names restored, his father's initials struck through. Emotional beat: sorrowful peace; the price of survival paid openly at last.

chapters.title: Will and Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Released on suspended sentence, he returns to a changed cathedral and a new register page left blank except for one line in his own hand: a will bequeathing the truth to whoever keeps the archive next. Emotional beat: hard-won hope—an inheritance rewritten as something worth receiving.
